pattern.top_pattern: Outpatient oncology and chemotherapy claims show a small but distinct mapping issue
pattern.what_is_impacting: CA / OH / OP IV Therapy-Oncology and OP Mgmt Oth Misc chemotherapy

providers: EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL
MERCY HEALTH- SAINT VINCENT MEDICAL CENTER

pattern.pattern_details: A small but recurring set of outpatient oncology and chemotherapy claims is appearing in CA and OH, with claims landing in not-mapped outpatient groupings. The dollars are modest, but oncology is a distinct pathway and should not be folded into general outpatient validation. Confirm chemotherapy coding and benefit assignment before any oncology authorization changes are considered.
pattern.why_it_matters: Even small oncology misclassification can create the wrong medical-versus-pharmacy policy response.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Have clinical and data-quality teams validate chemotherapy drug coding, regimen classification, and benefit assignment for the named providers before adjusting oncology authorization rules.
pattern.validation_reason: The pattern depends on chemotherapy claims landing in not-mapped outpatient groupings, so coding and benefit mapping must be checked first.
evidence_summary: CA/OH OP IV Therapy-Oncology added +$69K from four claims across EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL and MERCY HEALTH- SAINT VINCENT MEDICAL CENTER.
CA OP Mgmt Oth Misc chemotherapy added +$59K from three claims at EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL.
All supporting claims involved Chemotherapy Drugs and not-mapped outpatient grouping.
This is low volume but clinically distinct enough to warrant separate oncology validation.
